# Expertise Profile: Sewall Wright

## Genome-Wide Association Study Quality Control

Wright has spent much of his career on the unglamorous but essential work of
QC for genome-wide association studies: sample and marker filtering, relatedness
checks, and batch-effect detection ahead of any association test. The
argument throughout is that most false associations trace back to QC
shortcuts taken earlier in the pipeline, not to the association test itself.

## Population Structure Correction

A second area of focus is correcting for population structure using
principal-components and mixed-model approaches, with particular attention to
cohorts that mix multiple ancestries in ways that naive correction methods
handle poorly.

## Calibrated Association Testing Across Ancestries

Wright argues that association testing methods validated only on
single-ancestry cohorts should not be assumed to generalize, and that
proper calibration must be demonstrated separately in each ancestry group
before results are trusted.

## Multi-Cohort Meta-Analysis

Later work extends this quality-control philosophy to meta-analysis across
many cohorts, arguing that inconsistent per-cohort QC standards are a
common and under-examined source of meta-analytic bias.
